items.title: Runtime artifact projections are deferred and replayable
items.statement: The runtime-artifact family is a deferred, non-build-blocking redb projection with three project/artifact/checkpoint key shapes. Its checkpoint is disposable, its index follows artifact/evidence retention, its content is ref-only and redacted, and implementation authority requires family-specific schemas.

items.title: Worktree, lane, and thread projections preserve lineage
items.statement: The deferred worktree/lane/thread family is produced by Source Control and assistant-thread projectors for Assistant chat, Source Control, and Orchestrator. Bindings replay from chat events, lifecycle records retain lineage and tombstones, and paths may be normalized or redacted without storing local-machine secrets.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Thread/worktree bindings rebuild from chat.thread_worktree_* events; lane/worktree records retain lifecycle lineage.",
"retention_compaction": "Records retain archive/removed/deleted tombstones while historical links exist.",
"redaction_no_secret_rule": "Paths may be redacted or display-normalized; no local machine secrets may be stored.",

items.title: Attention and account projections are disposable or history-retained by class
items.statement: The deferred project-attention/account family rebuilds from events and runtime attribution. Attention projections are disposable, pressure and switch events follow account history retention, and provider/account identity is masked while authentication material is excluded.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Rebuild account/attention projections from events and runtime attribution records.",
"retention_compaction": "Attention projections are disposable; pressure/switch events retain according to account history policy.",
"redaction_no_secret_rule": "Account labels and provider identity are redacted/masked according to export policy; auth material is never stored.",

items.title: Provider runtime identity cannot launch until currentness is proven
items.statement: Provider runtime identity remains deferred. Discovery/currentness must be proven before launch, account-backed and server-profile-backed identity must be split, only masked identity references are stored, and the family reopens in the provider-stream tier.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Deferred; provider stream readiness must prove discovery/currentness before launch.",
"migration": "Must split account-backed and server-profile-backed runtime identity.",
"redaction_no_secret_rule": "Credentials and tokens remain in the OS credential store; this family stores masked identity refs only.",

items.title: Terminal workspace replay restores historical layout, not liveness
items.statement: The materialized terminal workspace row is keyed by project and workspace tab. It carries ordered section ids, nullable active ids, optional generation and budget reference, timestamps, and a no-secrets/redacted-refs profile. Replay is historical GUI restoration and cannot certify process liveness.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores terminal workspace layout and selected ids as historical GUI state only; replay never certifies terminal process liveness.",

items.title: Terminal sections persist ordering without process claims
items.statement: A materialized section row belongs to a workspace tab, stores title, ordered child terminal-tab ids, nullable active-tab id, collapsed state, timestamps, and redaction profile. Replay restores section and ordering only and does not assert child-process liveness.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores terminal sections and tab ordering without asserting that any child process is still alive.",

items.title: Terminal tabs restore metadata and pane roots for historical review
items.statement: A materialized terminal-tab row belongs to a section and stores a title, required pane-tree root, nullable active session, timestamps, and redaction profile. Replay restores metadata and the root only for historical layout review.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores tab metadata and pane-tree root for historical layout review only.",

items.title: Pane rows encode split-tree shape separately from liveness
items.statement: Each materialized pane row is either split or leaf, links to parent and children, and may carry split axis and size fraction. Replay restores the split tree but leaves leaf liveness to runtime validation.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores split tree layout; leaf liveness remains runtime-validated and is never inferred from this value.",

items.title: Leaf panes restore session references and require runtime revalidation or relaunch
items.statement: A materialized leaf-pane row requires pane and session ids plus cwd and shell-profile references. It may keep the last command-block id and a title. Replay restores the last-known session reference for history, while the runtime must separately revalidate or relaunch the process.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores the leaf pane's last known session reference for history; runtime must revalidate or relaunch any process separately.",
"redaction_no_secret_rule": "cwd and shell profile are refs only; raw paths with secrets, env values, and output buffers are forbidden.",

items.title: Terminal workgroups are grouping metadata only
items.statement: A materialized workgroup row groups workspace-tab ids under a title and optional description. Replay restores only named GUI grouping metadata, and retention lasts while a member workspace tab remains live.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores named terminal workgroups as GUI grouping metadata only.",
"retention_compaction": "Retain while any workspace tab id remains live; compact empty historical groups after policy retention.",

items.title: Cross-row referential integrity is unspecified
items.statement: The materialized schemas model section, tab, root-pane, child-pane, session, and workspace membership as unconstrained strings or arrays. The assigned window does not state existence, same-project, uniqueness, reciprocal-link, ordering-membership, or dangling-reference rules, nor the write behavior when one is violated.
items.impact: Builders can accept mutually inconsistent terminal trees and GUI selections, producing non-deterministic replay, orphan cleanup, and propagation behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Must choose validation timing, transaction boundaries, cascade/reject semantics, and repair behavior for dangling or cross-project references.

items.title: Pane topology invariants are absent
items.statement: The pane schema enumerates split and leaf kinds but applies the same parent, child, axis, and size fields to both without conditional constraints. The window does not define root cardinality, acyclicity, child count, parent-child reciprocity, leaf child prohibition, split-axis requirements, size bounds, or sibling-fraction normalization.
items.impact: Malformed or cyclic pane graphs can pass schema validation and make layout restoration, traversal, compaction, and GUI rendering ambiguous or unsafe.
items.builder_discretion: Must invent topology validation and normalization rules, including whether malformed stored trees are rejected, repaired, or partially displayed.

items.title: Runtime revalidation and relaunch failure behavior is unspecified
items.statement: The replay contract correctly separates historical GUI state from live process state, but it does not define the validation oracle, timeout, state transition, user-visible status, retry policy, fallback, or record mutation when a session is dead, missing, unauthorized, or cannot be relaunched.
items.impact: Different builders can expose stale sessions differently, accidentally imply liveness, loop relaunches, or lose historical state after a failed recovery.
items.builder_discretion: Must design the revalidation/relaunch state machine and GUI failure presentation.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Restores terminal workspace layout and selected ids as historical GUI state only; replay never certifies terminal process liveness.",
"replay_behavior": "Restores split tree layout; leaf liveness remains runtime-validated and is never inferred from this value.",
"replay_behavior": "Restores the leaf pane's last known session reference for history; runtime must revalidate or relaunch any process separately.",

items.title: Retention and compaction rules lack executable thresholds
items.statement: Retention prose is relationship-driven but leaves live, expire, orphaned, policy retention, referenced, and superseded undefined in the assigned window. It also omits grace periods, sweep ordering, atomic cascade behavior, crash recovery, and evidence that compaction cannot break retained history.
items.impact: Implementations can compact the same graph at different times or orders, retaining indefinitely or deleting still-navigable historical state.
items.builder_discretion: Must choose retention clocks, reachability rules, transaction scope, and compaction acceptance tests.

evidence.exact_quote: "retention_compaction": "Retain while the project workspace exists; compact superseded layout generations after referenced sessions and command blocks expire.",
"retention_compaction": "Retain while referenced by terminal_tab_record; compact orphaned panes after child/leaf rows expire.",
"retention_compaction": "Retain while any workspace tab id remains live; compact empty historical groups after policy retention.",

items.title: Legacy terminal migration has no deterministic procedure or oracle
items.statement: Each family states the intended split/import at a prose level, but the assigned window does not specify legacy version detection, id derivation, ordering preservation, collision handling, partial/corrupt input behavior, transactional rollback, idempotency, or post-migration equivalence checks.
items.impact: Builders can produce different ids and graphs from the same legacy blob or leave partially migrated data after interruption.
items.builder_discretion: Must invent migration mapping, failure semantics, transactionality, and fixtures/oracles.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "Legacy terminal bottom-panel blobs split into workspace, section, tab, pane, session, and command-block rows before implementation authority.",
"migration": "Imports legacy terminal section blobs into one section row per section id.",
"migration": "Splits legacy pane-tree blobs into one row per pane.",
"migration": "Splits terminal leaves from legacy terminal pane blobs.",

items.title: Free-form display metadata lacks enforceable no-secret validation
items.statement: The value schemas accept unconstrained title and description strings while prose forbids command output, credentials, and shell environment. A redaction-profile enum records an asserted mode but the assigned window provides no sanitizer, source restrictions, rejection behavior, length bound, or test oracle proving that these free-form fields obey it.
items.impact: Secret-bearing command or environment text can be persisted in display metadata despite the stated no-secret policy.
items.builder_discretion: Must determine trust boundaries, sanitization/redaction algorithms, rejection/fallback behavior, and validation fixtures.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "Workgroup metadata must not include command output, credentials, or raw shell environment.",

items.title: Timestamp ordering and update authority are unspecified
items.statement: Created and updated values are format-checked strings, but the assigned window does not define clock authority, monotonicity, created-at versus updated-at ordering, precision, skew handling, or conflict resolution for concurrent projector writes.
items.impact: Replay order, last-writer selection, migration equivalence, and retention age can diverge across implementations.
items.builder_discretion: Must choose time source, comparison rules, precision, and conflict behavior.

items.title: Canonical MessagePack acceptance oracle is not bound in the window
items.statement: All materialized terminal families name messagepack_canonical encoding and exact schema ids/versions, but the assigned window does not bind a canonicalization profile, decoder strictness, unknown-field behavior beyond value-schema validation, golden bytes, or round-trip oracle.
items.impact: Independent implementations may serialize map ordering, numeric values, or rejected inputs differently while claiming the same canonical encoding.
items.builder_discretion: Must choose or locate a canonical MessagePack profile and conformance fixtures before interoperable storage can be demonstrated.

items.title: Deferred grouped families are intentionally not implementation-authoritative
items.statement: The four grouped inventories explicitly identify themselves as deferred and non-build-blocking, provide deferred ownership/reasons/reopen conditions, and in relevant cases require owner-specific or family-specific schemas before implementation authority. Their generic optional fields should not be mistaken for executable schemas in this phase.

evidence.exact_quote: "deferred_reason": "Runtime artifact GUI projections are outside Tier 0C-2 launch-critical storage.",
"deferred_reason": "Worktree/lane GUI projections are not required to close Tier 0C-2 persistence blockers.",

items.title: Materialized terminal storage ownership and consumers are consistent
items.statement: All six materialized terminal families in the core assign storage-plan as owner, terminal and editor projectors as producer, and terminal GUI plus Runtime Artifacts panel as consumers.

dimension_assessments.summary: Replay, persistence, retention, migration, and redaction behaviors are extracted for every family in the core.
Deferred projector inventories and six materialized terminal GUI storage capabilities are identified.
Field shapes are explicit, but cross-row membership, topology, and temporal validity rules for accepted inputs and emitted stored graphs are incomplete.
Schema and replay contracts exist, while referential, topology, migration, and encoding conformance contracts remain underspecified in the assigned window.
Historical-versus-live state is distinguished, but dead-session detection, relaunch, retry, and failure transitions are not defined.
Deferred implementation authority and materialized family ownership/production authority are explicit.
Deferred owner docs are declared, and materialized terminal rows consistently name storage-plan with terminal/editor projectors.
Each family names consumers; terminal materialized rows consistently serve terminal GUI and Runtime Artifacts panel.
Workspace, section, tab, pane, leaf, and workgroup rows are historical GUI state and explicitly do not prove process liveness.
Runtime revalidation or relaunch is required but its failure/retry/fallback state machine is not specified.
Strong no-secret prose exists for all families, but unconstrained free-form display fields lack an enforceable sanitizer and oracle.
The row graph is described by ids, but propagation and cascade semantics for link changes, deletion, compaction, and active selections are not defined.
Replay and retention intent is present; executable recovery, compaction, migration, and concurrent timestamp operations remain open.
No bounds or operational budgets are given for ordered id arrays, graph size/depth, compaction batches, or replay cost in this window.
Legacy split/import destinations are named, but deterministic transforms, idempotency, rollback, and equivalence oracles are absent.
JSON value schemas provide field-level oracles, but there are no graph, migration, recovery, secret-scrubbing, timestamp, retention, or canonical-byte conformance oracles in the assigned window.
Consequential discretion remains over graph integrity, layout topology, recovery, compaction, migration, secret handling, time, and encoding.

The principal unknowns are bounded to the missing invariants and executable oracles identified by the gap items; deferred grouped families are explicitly non-authoritative rather than accidental omissions.
